posts.title: Inside Frensense 0.7.0: Package-Aware Dataflow, Compiler Purity, and Replay-Verified Static Analysis
posts.description: A deep technical dive into Frensense 0.7.0 - solving cross-framework false positives with package-scoped facts, decoupling AST vocabularies into pure compiler IR, and enforcing replay verification over the bundle's own corpus.

posts.title: Static Analysis in the Era of Frontier AI: Why LLMs Need Deterministic Oracles
posts.description: A deep technical examination of where static application security testing stands against models like Claude Opus 5.5 and Gemini 3.8 Flash, and why autonomous AI coding agents require compiler-mode deterministic verifiers like Frensense.

posts.title: Teaching a Static Analyzer Like a Human: Learning Detection from Twin Examples
posts.description: How Frensense replaced fragile pattern rules and hardcoded engine updates with a compiler that learns security vulnerabilities directly from positive and negative examples - and how every fact must prove itself before it ships.

posts.title: Frensense v2: the first preview
posts.description: Why we rebuilt the engine as a compiler, and what the first preview ships - memory-safety checkers, value-aware guards, and a corpus that teaches the engine.

posts.title: Proving guards, not guessing them
posts.description: Guard validation used to be textual, a call with the right name near the sink. The value lattice changed that - and has limits we state here.
